_comment: Generated by scripts/conformance_scoreboard.py — per-policy conformance drill-down for one jurisdiction. Do not hand-edit.

policies.note: State-pension-age adjustment (Comment 'DEF: Pension age adjustment - changes in earnings and pensions due to increase in the state pension age'; Type ben but a switch-type toggle). Its functions only *adjust input variables* for the SPA-rise counterfactual: for people below state pension age it subtracts the observed state pension (formula (-boact_s) into boact_s), swaps observed earnings/hours/ self-employment for imputed values (yem := yemiv, lhw00 := lhwiv00, yse := yseiv, output_add_var each), and re-derives lhw. It computes no distinct payable instrument — boact_s is written only to zero it out pre-SPA, not to pay a benefit. This is input-carrying (the InitVars pattern), not a scored surface; reclassified from the initial seed's in-scope guess (evidence: UK.xml UK_2026 PAA_uk function body).

BEN: benefit cap on Housing Benefit and Universal Credit (UC Regs 2013 reg 80A/81). bcap_uk computes the cap reduction, not a benefit: brd_s reduces the legacy-benefit stack (i_bcap_finalAmt = (bsa_s+bsadi_s+bho_s+bwkmt_s+bfamt_s) - brd_s) and brduc_s reduces UC (i_bcap_finalAmt += bsauc_s - brduc_s), each capped at the relevant award and gated by the reg-80A annual limits (single GBP 14,753 / couple-or-lone-parent GBP 22,020, London GBP 16,967 / 25,323) via amount#2/#4. Crucially, bcap_uk writes brd_s/brduc_s/bsadi02_s but does NOT write back into bsauc_s or bho_s: UKMOD reports the UNCAPPED award and carries the cap effect only in the separate reduction outputs (verified: no bcap_uk function outputs bsauc_s in UK_2026). Axiom encodes the UC benefit cap (reg 80A limits + reg 81 reduction: rulespec-uk uk/regulations/uksi/2013/376/80A and /81, whose output universal_credit_award_benefit_cap_reduction is the direct analog of UKMOD brduc_s) and applies it INSIDE the composed UC award before the s.8(1) award. So the uk-universal-credit suite's bsauc_s comparison surfaces the reporting divergence as an upstream_engine_gap (UKMOD does not apply the cap to hypothetical benefit units), but no live suite yet compares bcap_uk's own reduction output against Axiom's reg-81 reduction. Uncovered until a dedicated benefit-cap surface maps UKMOD brduc_s to universal_credit_award_benefit_cap_reduction (and brd_s to a legacy-benefit reduction, unencoded — the Axiom UC pilot is UC-only); requires the x64 UKMOD runtime to regenerate the report (rulespec-uk#57).

BEN: Child Benefit. The uk-child-benefit suite live-compares the composed UK Child Benefit pipeline (SSCBA 1992 s.141 with the SI 2006/965 reg.2 enhanced GBP 27.05 / other GBP 17.90 weekly rates, annualised over 52 weeks) against UKMOD's pre-charge Child Benefit on a single-parent grid (one/two/three children x 20k/70k/80k/90k straddling the HICBC taper), matching 12/12. The gross surface bridges to UKMOD by summing paid bch_s and the separately-reported charge clawback bchrd_s (UKMOD policy bchrd_uk nets the clawback into bch_s), so the summed [bch_s, bchrd_s] reconstructs the gross pre-charge entitlement — the parity target. The HICBC (ITEPA 2003 ss.681B-681H) is now corpus-grounded (axiom-corpus#221) and encoded on the Axiom side (rulespec-uk#84 closed #75), so the suite also wires a net-of-charge surface (bch_s alone vs Axiom's post-charge amount); the committed report exercises the gross bridge surface. The ~0.27% 52-vs-52.14-weeks convention residual is inside tolerance; all cases recover the same statutory weekly rates. bch_s is the compared surface, so bch_uk is covered.

BEN: Free School Meals (UKMOD comment "BEN: Free School Meals"), not a Child Benefit education-age extension despite the bch* prefix. bched01_s is a passported, means-tested devolved benefit: eligibility passports off receipt of other means-tested awards (bsa_s, bunmt_s, bsadi_s, bfamt_s/bwkmt_s with il_TC_means thresholds, bsauc_s with i_UC_means_earned_adj, boamtmm_s) crossed with primary/secondary age bands and region (drgn1=12 Scotland, drgn1=13 NI), valued at $BFSMprim / $BFSMsec and scaled by the take-up factors $BFSMPrUnTakeUp/$BFSMPrMtTakeUp/$BFSMScMtTakeUp. Not encoded in Axiom (no FSM pipeline in rulespec-uk), and the synthetic UK grids run drgn1=2, so no current case activates it. Groundability assessment (this-wave): FSM is not a standalone statutory rate-and-threshold rule that grounds cleanly like the Scottish Child Payment — it is a passported service (Education (Scotland) Act 1980 s.53-55 powers; devolved Scottish/NI administration) whose eligibility is derived from receipt of the upstream means-tested benefits and whose rate is set administratively and take-up-scaled. Encoding it therefore requires the upstream benefits (UC/IS/JSA/ESA/HB/PC) encoded first plus a non-standard derived-entitlement layer, not a self-contained corpus ingest. Uncovered; the honest build path is a passported surface (region/passporting inputs) layered on those upstream awards, not encoder-first from a single statute. Out of scope for the child-benefit + benefit-cap lane.

BEN: School Clothing Grant (UKMOD comment "BEN: School Clothing Grant"), not a Child Benefit education-age extension despite the bch* prefix. bched02_s passports off the same means-tested awards as bched01_uk (bsa_s/bunmt_s/bsadi_s/bfamt_s/bwkmt_s/bsauc_s/boamtmm_s) for dependent children aged 12-18 (dec!=6, dec!=0) at the secondary grant rate $BScSCGsec. A passported devolved payment, not encoded in Axiom; the synthetic UK grids run drgn1=2 so no current case activates it. Groundability assessment (this-wave): like FSM (bched01_uk), the School Clothing Grant is a passported, take-up-scaled, administratively-set Scottish service, not a clean standalone statutory rate — it grounds only on top of the upstream means-tested awards it passports off, so it needs those encoded first plus a derived-entitlement layer, not encoder-first from a single statute. Uncovered; the honest build path is a passported surface on those upstream awards. Out of scope for the child-benefit + benefit-cap lane.

BEN: Child Winter Heating Assistance (Scotland) (UKMOD comment "BEN: Child Winter Heating Assistance (Scotland)"), not a Child Benefit household/HICBC test component despite the bch* prefix. bchht_s is a devolved Scottish disability payment: paid at $SCWHA to a child under 18 in Scotland (drgn1=12) whose highest-rate DLA/PIP care indicator (i_bdisc01 or i_bdiscwa01) reaches $DLACareHigh*0.95. The CWHA payment itself is not encoded in Axiom, and the synthetic UK grids run drgn1=2 with no disability inputs, so no current case activates it. Groundability assessment (this-wave): CWHA is the readiest of the three devolved bch* rows to encode — it is a clean flat-rate top-up (not a take-up-scaled passported service like FSM/School Clothing), its disability passport is ALREADY encoded (rulespec-uk uk/policies/govuk/disability-living-allowance.yaml and personal-independence-payment.yaml, WRA 2012 ss.77-79), and its gating care indicators (bdisc, bdiscwa) are admissible columns of the training_data schema. Uncovered until the flat CWHA amount (Scotland, child under 18, highest-rate care) is encoded on top of that passport and a Scotland/disability surface is built with the care inputs supplied; requires the x64 UKMOD runtime to regenerate. Out of scope for the child-benefit + benefit-cap lane.
Scottish Child Payment bridging payments: every function n/a in UK_2026 — the transitional bridging scheme has ended.

BEN: Scottish Child Payment (UKMOD comment "BEN: Child Payment (Scotland)"), not a Child Benefit means-test variant despite the bch* prefix (distinct from the excluded bchmt01_uk SCP bridging scheme). bchmt_s is a devolved Scotland-only (drgn1=12) means-tested payment: eligibility passports off il_bchmt (the summed qualifying awards boamt_s+bsadi_s+bunmt_s+bsa_s+bwkmt_s+bfamt_s+bsauc_s) with dependent children in the benefit unit, and the final BenCalc consumes UKMOD's stochastic take-up draw (i_rand_tu<=$SCPTUu6y for children under 6 / <=$SCPTU6to15y for 6-15, switch=switch) so the reported bchmt_s is take-up-adjusted away from the statutory entitlement — the same take-up-draw exposure documented for bsauc_s. Axiom DOES encode the Scottish Child Payment (rulespec-uk uk/policies/govuk/scottish-child-payment.yaml, SSI 2020/351 regs 18/20, output scottish_child_payment_annual_amount = weekly amount * weeks_in_year, gated on person_lives_in_scotland and child_age<max_age and applicant_or_partner_receives_qualifying_benefit), so the prior "not encoded" note was stale. It is uncovered only because the synthetic UK grids run drgn1=2, so no current case activates it. Build path (child-benefit-style Scotland surface): a benefit-unit grid routed to Scotland (drgn1=12) that produces a qualifying means-tested award so UKMOD's il_bchmt fires, comparing scottish_child_payment_annual_amount against bchmt_s with the take-up constants pinned to 1.0 via euromod_constant_overrides ($SCPTUu6y/$SCPTU6to15y, per the #168 study-allowance/UC-PC take-up-pinning pattern) so bchmt_s reports the statutory entitlement; requires the x64 UKMOD runtime to regenerate. Out of scope for the child-benefit + benefit-cap lane.

BEN: Reduce child benefit (from 2013) — the High Income Child Benefit Charge clawback (ITEPA 2003 ss.681B-681H). bchrd_uk computes bchrd_s = ((adjusted_net_income - $ITCBthresh)/200)*1% * bch_s, capped at bch_s, then nets bchrd_s back into bch_s (UK_2026: threshold GBP 60,000, full clawback at GBP 80,000). The uk-child-benefit suite live-compares the composed Axiom Child Benefit pipeline against UKMOD's gross pre-charge entitlement whose euromod target is the summed list [bch_s, bchrd_s] — so bchrd_uk's distinct output bchrd_s is exercised as a summand of the compared surface (matching 12/12 on the single-parent grid whose income sweep 20k/70k/80k/90k straddles the taper). The HICBC is now corpus-grounded (axiom-corpus#221) and encoded on the Axiom side (rulespec-uk#84 closed #75), so a direct net-of-charge surface (bch_s alone vs Axiom's post-charge entitlement) is wired into the suite too; the committed report exercises the gross bridge surface, which already consumes bchrd_s. bchrd_s is a compared surface, so bchrd_uk is covered — mirroring bch_uk.

BEN: Scottish Carer's Allowance Supplement (from Sept 2018). The UK_2026 policy is switch=on and computes a distinct payable instrument bcrdicm_s = the flat weekly supplement $CASupW, gated on being a Carer's Allowance recipient in Scotland (Elig_Cond (bcrdi>0) & (drgn1=12)); it then sums bcrdi + bcrdicm_s into i_bcrdi for downstream means tests. It is a genuine comparable surface (a flat supplement on a Scottish-carer case), NOT input-carrying — distinct from the boact_uk/PAA_uk uprating- passthrough exclusions. Two properties bound its comparability: (i) eligibility keys off bcrdi, the reported Carer's Allowance data input — which IS an admissible column of the registration-free training_data schema (verified: bcrdi present in Input/training_data.txt), so a supplied-receipt synthetic case (bcrdi>0, drgn1=12) can fire the supplement (this is NOT an oracle_dataset_lacks_input case — the activating input exists); (ii) it is a devolved Scotland-only payment. The encoding blocker is Axiom-side: rulespec-uk does not encode the supplement (no Social Security (Scotland) Act 2018, asp 9, s.70-74 CAS surface), and the supplement passports off Carer's Allowance, which is itself unencoded (rulespec-uk#55, SSCBA 1992 s.70) — so CAS needs CA encoded first, then the flat weekly supplement layered on a Scottish-carer case. Uncovered next-wave surface pending that encoding; the supplied-receipt grid + x64 UKMOD regen make it gradable once encoded (evidence: UK.xml UK_2026 bcrdicm_uk function body; training_data.txt bcrdi column; rulespec-uk#55).
Adjusts existing disability-benefit inputs (bdisc/bdimb/…) rather than computing a distinct instrument; its only near-output (receive_pip_s) is an imputed-input flag, not a payable amount.
Adjusts the number of DLA recipients post-2011 (a recipient reweighting), not a distinct payable benefit; writes no queryable _s output in UK_2026.

BEN: Housing Benefit. The UK_2026 policy is switch=on and computes the full HB entitlement bho_s from statute: applicable amount (personal allowances i_bho_PersAllow by age/couple/lone-parent status + disability/carer/family premiums + child element with the two-child limit), the means test ymn01_s, the 65% taper of excess income over the applicable amount, maximum HB = eligible rent (xhcrt + xhcsc) less non-dependant deductions, and the size-criteria (bedroom-tax) 14%/25% reduction for i_excess_nRooms excess rooms. This is a genuine benefit-unit comparable surface: rulespec-uk encodes the composed HB entitlement pipeline (housing_benefit_composed_entitlement_pipeline, rulespec-uk#83), so bho_s is the parity target on synthetic HHoT renter cases (rent/tenure supplied through the projection layer's xhcrt/xhcsc + amrtn, bedroom counts through amrrm/bhoro). The uk-housing-benefit suite builds that comparison: single/couple, working-age/pension-age renters, an earnings sweep crossing the 65% taper, and a non-dependant-deduction case, bridging UKMOD's assessed HB means ymn01_s into the pipeline's applicable income so both engines taper the identical income (the bho_s award formula i_bho_maxHousBen - 0.65*(ymn01_s - i_bho_prelimAmt) mirrors the pipeline's rent_after_taper less non-dependant deductions). Like UC/PC/ir-ESA, bho_s embeds UKMOD's take-up correction (the "fully random" i_bho_probtu group gate on i_rand_tu against $HBTUWAWork/$HBTUWANowork/$HBTUPen, and a "based on observed take-up" path that gates on the bho data input, absent on synthetic households) and a UC-transition that can zero a would-be award away from statutory entitlement; the clean pre-correction value is i_bho_noUC. The comparison spec pins those take-up rates to 1.0 via euromod_constant_overrides (or#168) so a runner regeneration returns statutory entitlements, disposing any residual zeros upstream_engine_gap (recharacterization per or#168/or#170). Uncovered until the x64 runner emits the committed report (UKMOD has no macOS wheel; scripts/regenerate_euromod_uk.sh is the source of the numbers) (evidence: UK.xml UK_2026 bho_uk function body).

BEN: Discretionary Housing Payments (Scotland) — bedroom-tax mitigation. Verdict: scoped out (not encoded), a modelled policy assumption rather than a statutory formula. The UK_2026 policy is switch=on and computes a distinct payable bhosc01_s: for a Scottish social renter (amrtn=5 & drgn1=12 & dhr=1) subject to the bedroom tax it pays back the size-criteria reduction (14% of (xhcrt + xhcsc) for one excess room, 25% for more), gated on being on HB (bho_s>0) or UC (bsauc_s>0), plus a benefit-cap top-up limited to housing costs xhc_hbai. UKMOD models this as if formulaic, but the underlying instrument is not: DHPs rest on the Discretionary Financial Assistance Regulations 2001 (SI 2001/1167) reg 2(2), which gives the relevant authority a discretion "as to whether or not to make discretionary housing payments in a particular case; and as to the amount of the payments" — no statutory formula, percentage, or cap. Administered by the 32 Scottish local authorities and demand-led/budget-capped (the Scottish Government funds full bedroom-tax mitigation as a policy commitment, not a statutory entitlement to a fixed amount). The only statutory numbers UKMOD uses here (14%/25%) are the HB/UC size-criteria percentages, already encoded where they ARE statutory: rulespec-uk uk/regulations/uksi/2013/376/schedule/4/paragraph/36 (Universal Credit under-occupancy: 0.14 one excess bedroom, 0.25 two or more). So encoding "pay back 14%/25% of eligible rent" as if a Scottish statutory formula would misrepresent a discretionary, LA-administered, budget-capped payment (and the corpus carries no DHP source to ground it). Kept in scope as a real UKMOD surface but classified not-comparable-from-statute; the size-criteria percentages it references are already covered on the UC side (evidence: UK.xml UK_2026 bhosc01_uk function body; SI 2001/1167 reg 2(2)).

BEN: Statutory Maternity Pay. The UKMOD Comment says "(not simulated in the baseline)", but the UK_2026 policy is switch=on and computes bmact_s from ordinary demographic/earnings inputs — female (dgn=0) with a newborn (dag<1, baby-months dmb), earnings above the SMP lower-earnings-limit ($SMPlel), working hours (liwwh>6), and previous earnings i_yempv_bmact — with the 90%/flat-rate SMP formula over i_durweeks_bmact2. Confirmed empirically against UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03/UK_2026: bmact_s is nonzero and earnings-responsive on synthetic HHoT cases (lone mother, annual gross £8k->£5,370.49, £25k->£16,782.79, below the £130 LEL->£0), reconstructed exactly by the composed rulespec-uk SMP pipeline (SSCBA 1992 Part XII ss.164-166). Now COVERED by the uk-statutory-maternity-pay suite (5 cases, 5/5 match). UKMOD applies the earnings-related 90% rate over the full 39-week period for the HHoT case rather than the flat prescribed rate. bmact_uk does not consume the stochastic take-up draw i_rand_tu.

BEN: Healthy Start food voucher (rest of UK). Unlike the statutory-pay policies this is a passported means-tested payment: the Elig_Cond requires a qualifying means-tested benefit in payment (bsa_s>0 | bunmt_s>0 | boamt_s>0 | bfamt_s>0 | bsauc_s>0 ...), and the amount is $HSFood (£4.25/week per eligible child, doubled to £8.50/week for a child under one, 2026-27). Confirmed computable against UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03/UK_2026: for a zero-earnings lone parent with a newborn who is passported onto Universal Credit (bsauc_s>0, take-up pinned on via euromod_constant_overrides $ISTUNochild/$ISTUChild=1.0), bmamt01_s=£443.21. It does NOT consume the stochastic i_rand_tu take-up draw, so it is a deterministic passported surface. Now COVERED by the uk-healthy-start suite (2 cases, 2/2 match): the composed rulespec-uk pilot (SI 2005/3262 reg.8) annualises the determined weekly value over 52 benefit weeks, about 0.27% below UKMOD's 365/7 convention, within the 0.3% relative tolerance.

BEN: Sure Start Maternity Grant (rest of UK). Passported means-tested lump sum: the Elig_Cond requires a qualifying means-tested benefit in payment (bsa_s>0 | bunmt_s>0 | boamt_s>0 | bsauc_s>0 ...) and a child under 1 with no other dependent children, paying $BSurMaG (£500, 2026-27). Confirmed computable against UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03/UK_2026: for a zero-earnings lone parent with a newborn passported onto Universal Credit (bsauc_s>0, take-up pinned on via euromod_constant_overrides $ISTUNochild/$ISTUChild=1.0), bmamt_s=£500.00 (= $BSurMaG). It does NOT consume the stochastic i_rand_tu take-up draw, so it is a deterministic passported surface. Now COVERED by the uk-sure-start-maternity-grant suite (1 case, 1/1 match): the composed rulespec-uk pilot (SI 2005/3061 reg.5) exposes the £500 lump sum as a Person-level annual entitlement, matching to the penny.

BEN: Maternity Allowance. The UKMOD Comment says "(not simulated in the baseline)", but the UK_2026 policy is switch=on and computes bmanc_s from ordinary demographic/earnings inputs (eligible parent, newborn age-weeks, duration weeks, previous earnings i_yempv_bmanc). Maternity Allowance is payable only where Statutory Maternity Pay is not (Comp_Cond requires bmact_s=0), so it is exercised with a self-employed lone mother (yse>0, yem=0). Confirmed empirically against UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03/UK_2026: bmanc_s is nonzero and earnings-responsive (self-employment £9k->£6,041.80, £15k->£10,069.67), reconstructed exactly by the composed rulespec-uk MA pipeline (SSCBA 1992 Part II ss.35/35A/35B). Now COVERED by the uk-maternity-allowance suite (3 cases, 3/3 match). bmanc_uk does not consume the stochastic take-up draw.

BEN: Best Start Foods (Scotland). Passported means-tested payment: the Elig_Cond requires a qualifying means-tested benefit in payment (bsa_s>0 | bunmt_s>0 | boamt_s>0 | bsauc_s>0 ...) AND Scottish residence (drgn1=12), paying $BScBSF0 (£11.20/week under 1) or $BScBSF1to2 (£5.60/week ages 1-3), 2026-27. Confirmed computable against UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03/UK_2026: for a zero-earnings lone parent in Scotland (drgn1=12) with a newborn passported onto Universal Credit (bsauc_s>0, take-up pinned on via euromod_constant_overrides $ISTUNochild/$ISTUChild=1.0), bmascmt01_s=£584.00. Unlike its sibling bmascmt_uk (Best Start Grant), Best Start Foods does NOT consume the stochastic i_rand_tu take-up draw, so it is a deterministic passported surface. Now COVERED by the uk-best-start-foods suite (2 cases, 2/2 match): the composed rulespec-uk pilot (SSI 2019/193 reg.13, £5.60 basic rate per SSI 2026/170) annualises the weekly value over 52 benefit weeks, about 0.27% below UKMOD's 365/7 convention, within the 0.3% relative tolerance.

BEN: Best Start Grant (Scotland — Pregnancy and Baby, Early Learning, School Age payments). RECATEGORIZED to takeup_adjustment on probe evidence. Each component BenCalc gates the award on the stochastic per-benefit-unit take-up draw i_rand_tu (Comp_Cond i_rand_tu<=$BSGfirst / $BSGsec / $BSGearly / $BSGschool, with $BSGfirst commented "Take-up estimate: Best Start Grant pregnancy and baby take-up"), the same random-draw device UKMOD applies to Universal Credit (see BTA_uk / random_uk and euromod_issues.json ukmod-uc-bsauc-takeup-stochastic-zeroing). Verified live against UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03/UK_2026: for a passported Scottish lone parent (bsauc_s>0, take-up gate off) bmascmt_s=£0.00 — the draw does not pass — whereas overriding the take-up constants ($BSGfirst.. = 1) recovers the deterministic statutory amount bmascmt_s=£796.65 (= $BScStGFirstbaby). Because the baseline award is a stochastic draw, not a reproducible per-household statutory result, this is a take-up-adjustment surface (like the excluded BTA_uk), not a clean arithmetic oracle. Distinct from the sibling bmascmt01_uk (Best Start Foods), which has no take-up gate and stays in scope.

UKMOD Country Report §2.5.6: Council Tax Reduction is a deliberately simplified national scheme; post-2013 local heterogeneity is 'not reflected'. The applicable amount (i_bmu_prelimAmt) and non-dependant deductions (i_bmu_Deductions2) are i_-locals absent from VARCONFIG; only bmu_s/ymn01_s are queryable, so no non-degenerate comparison is possible. rulespec-uk encodes the SI 2012/2885 pension-age prescribed scheme taking exactly those internals as inputs.

State Pension (contributory). UKMOD does not compute the state pension from contribution records — its whole UK_2026 body is boact_s = boact00 * (SPSingle/SPSingle0): it takes the reported state- pension data input boact00 and applies an uprating factor. This is an uprating passthrough of a data input, computing no distinct entitlement from statute, so it is input-carrying, not a scored surface. Confirmed by the uk-pension-credit suite, whose live worker verifies "the boact_uk policy only uprates the boact00 state-pension data input" and feeds boact_s as an income-test input rather than a parity target. Reclassified from the initial seed's in-scope guess (evidence: UK.xml UK_2026 boact_uk body).

BEN: Pensioner's annual heating allowance (Winter Fuel Payment). The UK_2026 policy is switch=on and computes a distinct payable boaht_s at benefit-unit level: a base amount if anyone in the unit is of state-pension age ($WFA, with an additional $WFAAdd80 where anyone is 80+), on separate England/Wales (drgn1!=12) and Scotland (drgn1=12, $WFASc/$WFAAdd80Sc) branches from 2025, then allocated across pension-age members. It reflects the 2024/25 means-testing reform: every BenCalc comp_Cond now carries il_toty < amount#3 ($WFCBThresh) so the payment is withdrawn above the income claw-back threshold — the policy is no longer a universal pensioner payment. It is a genuine comparable surface (a household age + income-threshold gate on synthetic pensioner cases; no leave-spell or receipt-history column required). rulespec-uk encodes the England/Wales amounts in the Social Fund Winter Fuel Payment Regulations 2025 (SI 2025/969 reg 3: GBP 200 under-80, GBP 300 at-80), matching UKMOD's $WFA (200) + $WFAAdd80 (100). Uncovered because there is not yet a composed winter-fuel award pipeline wiring the means-test gate + age branches into a boaht_s parity target; the encoded reg-3 amounts are the building block. Next-wave uncovered surface (evidence: UK.xml UK_2026 boaht_uk function body and ConstDef_uk $WFA/$WFAAdd80/$WFASc/$WFCBThresh).

BEN: Statutory Paternity Pay. The UKMOD Comment says "(not simulated in the baseline)", but the UK_2026 policy is switch=on and computes bpact_s from ordinary inputs (eligible parent, previous earnings i_yempv_bpact). Confirmed empirically against UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03/UK_2026: bpact_s is nonzero and earnings-responsive on synthetic HHoT cases (lone father, annual gross £8k->£275.41, £25k->£860.66, below the £130 LEL->£0), reconstructed exactly by the composed rulespec-uk SPP pipeline (SSCBA 1992 Part 12ZA ss.171ZA/171ZE/171ZJ). Now COVERED by the uk-statutory-paternity-pay suite (5 cases, 5/5 match). UKMOD applies the earnings-related 90% rate over the 2-week period for the HHoT case. bpact_uk does not consume the stochastic take-up draw.

BEN: Social Assistance (income-based JSA, Income Support and Pension Credit). UKMOD computes Pension Credit inside this policy — boamt_s = guarantee credit boamtmm_s + savings credit boamtxp_s. The uk-pension-credit suite live-compares boamt_s against the composed RuleSpec guarantee-credit award (State Pension Credit Act 2002 s.2 + SPC Regs 2002 reg.6 standard-minimum-guarantee) on a single/couple pensioner grid crossing the guarantee level; the standard minimum guarantee matches to the penny (single 238.00/wk, couple 363.25/wk). boamt_s embeds a take-up / UC-transition correction that can zero a hypothetical award away from entitlement (ukmod-pc-boamt-takeup-transition); those points are dispositioned upstream_engine_gap, so unexplained=0 and Axiom-attributed=0 and the surface is covered. (JSA/IS legs of bsa_uk are separate uncovered surfaces; Pension Credit boamt_s is the compared one.)

BEN: Social Assistance (income-related Employment and Support Allowance). PROBE-ADJUDICATED (live UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03/UK_2026 on this Mac, x86_64/coreclr, euromod 0.2.18): the policy is switch=on and SIMULATES the full ir-ESA entitlement bsadi_s from statute — NOT a design-zero exclusion. With the limited-capability-for-work input supplied and the UC-transition constant $UCtransition set to 0 (Full Legacy Benefits) and take-up pinned, bsadi_s fires nonzero: ddipd=1 (WRAG) -> 6,961.07/yr (bsadi01_s WRAG component 1,978.82); ddipd=3 (Support) -> 7,607.64/yr (bsadi00_s Support 2,625.39); ddipd=0 -> 0 (falls back to Income Support bsa_s 4,982.25). It is a genuine benefit-unit comparable surface (applicable amount i_bsadi_PersAllow + SDP/carer/EDP premiums, LCW gate, il_IS_means means deduction, housing-cost non-dependant deductions, Support/WRAG components $ESAsup/$ESAwra). THREE barriers to a live UKMOD suite on the registration-free demo data, all evidenced: (1) the LCW eligibility gate reads ((ddipd>0)|(ddipd00>0)|((ddi02>=9)&(ddi02<=14))) and ddipd/ddipd00/ddi02 are pure data inputs ABSENT from the 365-column training_data schema (the _runner.py template overlay drops non-header columns) — ir-ESA cannot fire from statute on stock demo data (data-exercisability limit, like the PC savings-credit; a patched schema supplying ddipd exercises it, verified above); (2) the UC-transition (i_rand_uc<=$UCtransition; $UCtransition=0.06 baseline per DefConst, 0=LBA/1=UCA) plus the fully-random take-up ($ISTUChild=0.89/$ISTUNochild=0.83) can zero a hypothetical award away from entitlement (clean pre-transition value = i_bsadi_noUC) — dispositions upstream_engine_gap per or#168/or#170; (3) UK_2026 applies a FROZEN applicable amount ($ISSing25=73.10/wk vs the current statutory ESA Regs 2008 SI 2008/794 Sch 4 single-25+/main-phase 97.75/wk, corpus 2026-04-06 in force; UKMOD across systems 73.10(x4 incl UK_2026)..92.05,95.55,97.55.. = UK_2026 frozen ~2015 vintage), so an Axiom pipeline at current statutory rates would diverge from UKMOD by the freeze. Income-related ESA remains a LIVE legacy benefit in current law (closing to new claims via UC managed migration; existing awards continue). rulespec-uk does not yet encode ir-ESA. Statutory provisions ingested to axiom-corpus (2026-07-06-uk-esa-income-related: SI 2008/794 regs 67-68 + Sch 4). BEN: Contributory unemployment benefit (contribution-based Jobseeker's Allowance). The UK_2026 policy is switch=on and, once eligible, computes a distinct payable bunct_s from statute (age-banded rate $JSARate1824/$JSARate withdrawn pound-for-pound against the pension/earnings disregard base i_bunct_IncDisregard) — so it is NOT input-carrying. But eligibility is data-gated on the reported benefit-receipt input: the "eligibility fully simulated" Elig function is switch=OFF (its own comment warns it "will SEVERELY overestimate eligibility"), and the active path derives the qualifying-months variable liwmy_s from (bunct>0) receipt or an (les=5) unemployment status plus a liwwh work-history threshold, then gates the final Elig on liwmy_s>=$UB_QperMin. The activating inputs ARE admissible columns of the registration-free training_data schema (verified: bunct and liwwh both present in Input/training_data.txt; liwmy_s is derived, not a raw column), so this is NOT an oracle_dataset_lacks_input case — the current synthetic grids simply set them to non-activating values (no receipt, drgn1=2). A supplied-receipt/history case (bunct>0 or les=5 with liwwh above the work-history threshold) fires bunct_s from statute, so the surface is comparable for those cases (testing UKMOD's rate and withdrawal arithmetic, not its eligibility). The encoding blocker is Axiom-side: rulespec-uk does not encode contributory JSA (only the income-based JSA capital tariff, uksi/1996/207/116; the contributory scheme itself — Jobseekers Act 1995, age-banded flat rates $JSARate1824/$JSARate with pound-for-pound earnings withdrawal — is unencoded, adjacent to rulespec-uk#53). Uncovered next-wave surface, comparable under supplied-receipt cases once the contributory rates are encoded (evidence: UK.xml UK_2026 bunct_uk function body + verbatim "SEVERELY overestimate eligibility" switch-off comment; training_data.txt bunct/liwwh columns; rulespec-uk#53).

BEN: Tax credits (Working Tax Credit and Child Tax Credit). PROBE-ADJUDICATED (live UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03/UK_2026 on this Mac): the policy is switch=on and SIMULATES the full legacy tax-credit entitlements from statute — NOT a design-zero exclusion of the UKMOD row. With les=2 (employed) + lhw01 populated + $UCtransition=0 + take-up pinned, the surfaces fire nonzero: single childless 30h -> WTC bwkmt_s 3,145.95/yr (30-hour element bwkmtcm_s 1,070); lone parent 30h + 1 child -> WTC 5,780.95 + CTC bfamt_s 3,650 (CTC responds to child age: 3,650 age5 -> 4,195 age10); lone parent 16h -> WTC 5,205 (no 30h element, correct). WTC (basic/lone-parent/couple/30h/disability + 70%-of-xcc childcare) and CTC (family + per-child + disability, two-child limit) are jointly income-tested; the shared withdrawal (rate 0.41, threshold $WTCCTCThresh1) is applied to WTC FIRST then CTC (i_bwkmt_bfamt_withdrawnAmt). BUT: (1) THE BENEFIT IS ABOLISHED IN CURRENT LAW — Working Tax Credit and Child Tax Credit ENDED 5 April 2025 (gov.uk/tax-credits-have-ended; HoC Library CBP-9984); PolicyEngine encodes gov.dwp.tax_credits.active=false from 2025-04-06 and pays 0 in 2026 by design. UKMOD UK_2026 models a FROZEN CLOSING LEGACY STOCK, a counterfactual, not current law: $WTCBasic=1,960/yr vs the unrepealed-but-closed SI 2002/2005 Sch 2 basic 2,435 (corpus 2026-04-06) and the PE-projected 2,542. (2) take-up (switch-type fully-random, $WTCCTCTULP=0.96 etc.) + UC-transition zero hypothetical awards (clean pre-transition i_bwkmt_noUC/i_bfamt_noUC) — dispositions per or#168/or#170. Because the programme no longer pays ongoing awards, NO net-new statutory pipeline is encoded (it would encode dead law and grade a frozen UKMOD counterfactual); the row stays in-scope (UKMOD simulates it) with this probe evidence. Statutory rate provisions ingested to axiom-corpus anyway (2026-07-06-uk-tax-credits-rates: SI 2002/2005 Sch 2, SI 2002/2007 regs 7-8, SI 2002/2008 regs 7-8) for provenance. Evidence: UK.xml UK_2026 bwkmt_bfamt_uk function body; live probe 2026-07-06.

TAX: Personal tax allowance. The UK_2026 policy is switch=on and computes the final personal allowance tinta_s = preliminary allowance $ITPerAll less the income-limit taper (half of taxable income il_tinty in excess of $ITAllLim, floored at zero) — i.e. the Income Tax Act 2007 s.35(1)-(3) allowance with its adjusted-net-income withdrawal. This is a genuine, cleanly comparable surface: it needs only an income sweep on a single individual (no household structure, receipt history, or take-up draw), so it is the most directly gradable of the uncovered UK surfaces. rulespec-uk encodes exactly this computation — uk_pit_pilot_personal_allowance in pilot_worker_oracle_pipeline is ceil(max(0, personal_allowance_base_amount - max(0, adjusted_net_income - adjusted_net_income_reduction_threshold)/2)) against ITA 2007 s.35. The uk-personal-allowance suite now surfaces uk_pit_pilot_personal_allowance against tinta_s directly on a single-individual sweep (40k/100k/110k/125.14k/150k straddling the taper and full withdrawal); the concept mapping binds it to euromod tinta_s, and the comparison (comparisons/uk-personal-allowance-ukmod.yaml) regenerates on the x64 UKMOD runner via scripts/regenerate_euromod_uk.sh. Covered once that runner commits axiom-euromod-uk-personal-allowance.json (the euromod runtime has no macOS wheel, so the live match rate is generated on the provisioned runner, per axiom-oracles#190). Evidence: UK.xml UK_2026 tinta_uk function body; rulespec-uk s.35 encoding.
